item.research_question: How does the halogen-induced p-band center regulation affect the performance of lithium-sulfur batteries?
item.material_system: Cs2SnX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) halide perovskites
item.processing_route: Hydrothermal method, followed by ball-milling to reduce particle size
item.test_conditions: Room temperature, various current rates (0.2-5C), high sulfur loading (6.1 mg cm−2), low electrolyte/sulfur ratio (5.5 μL mg−1), and wide temperature range (−20 to 50 °C)
key_findings: The p-band center of halogen anions shifts positively toward the Fermi level with increasing halogen atomic number
Cs2SnI6 exhibits the highest electrical conductivity and electrocatalytic activity among the three samples
The Cs2SnI6 battery shows a high initial capacity of 1000 mA h g−1 at 2C and a low decay rate of 0.068% per cycle after 500 cycles
Cs2SnI6 achieves a remarkable reversible capacity of 768.8 mA h g−1 at a high sulfur loading and low E/S ratio
The Cs2SnI6 battery exhibits excellent cycling stability and rate performance, even at extreme temperatures
item.mechanism: The halogen-induced p-band center regulation enhances the electron transfer ability and strengthens the binding energy between Cs2SnI6 and LiPSs, leading to improved adsorption and catalytic performance
quotes: the p-band center of halogen anions shifted positively toward the Fermi level with the increase in the halogen atomic number
Cs2SnI6 is intrinsically endowed with superb adsorptive and catalytic activity and redox kinetics of lithium polysulfides

Processing: Hydrothermal method, followed by ball-milling to reduce particle size. Test conditions: Room temperature, various current rates (0.2-5C), high sulfur loading (6.1 mg cm−2), low electrolyte/sulfur ratio (5.5 μL mg−1), and wide temperature range (−20 to 50 °C). Findings: The p-band center of halogen anions shifts positively toward the Fermi level with increasing halogen atomic number; Cs2SnI6 exhibits the highest electrical conductivity and electrocatalytic activity among the three samples; The Cs2SnI6 battery shows a high initial capacity of 1000 mA h g−1 at 2C and a low decay rate of 0.068% per cycle after 500 cycles; Cs2SnI6 achieves a remarkable reversible capacity of 768.8 mA h g−1 at a high sulfur loading and low E/S ratio; The Cs2SnI6 battery exhibits excellent cycling stability and rate performance, even at extreme temperatures. Mechanism: The halogen-induced p-band center regulation enhances the electron transfer ability and strengthens the binding energy between Cs2SnI6 and LiPSs, leading to improved adsorption and catalytic performance. Quote: "the p-band center of halogen anions shifted positively toward the Fermi level with the increase in the halogen atomic number"

item.research_question: How do halogen-induced p-band centers regulate the adsorption and catalytic performance of lithium–sulfur batteries?
key_findings: High discharge capacity (1000 mA h g−1 at 2C)
Excellent rate performance (771.0 mA h g−1 at 5C)
Long-term cycle stability (0.068% decay rate per cycle after 500 cycles at 2C)
High discharge capacity at extreme temperatures (912.7 mA h g−1 at 0.1C at −20 °C and 1350.7 mA h g−1 at 0.5C at 50 °C)
item.mechanism: The p-band center of the halogen anion shifts positively toward the Fermi level as the atomic number of the halogen increases, resulting in a higher charge transfer rate and promoting the kinetics of the conversion reaction of LiPSs
quotes: the regulatory mechanism of halogen-induced p-band centers and their effects on the adsorption and catalytic performance of LSBs were successfully explored
the p-band center of the halogen anion shifted positively toward the Fermi level
providing a new approach for developing advanced LSBs through halogen-induced p-band center regulation engineering

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do halogen-induced p-band centers regulate the adsorption and catalytic performance of lithium–sulfur batteries?. System: Sn-based halide perovskites, specifically Cs2SnI6. Test conditions: 2C, 5C, 0.1C at −20 °C, 0.5C at 50 °C. Findings: High discharge capacity (1000 mA h g−1 at 2C); Excellent rate performance (771.0 mA h g−1 at 5C); Long-term cycle stability (0.068% decay rate per cycle after 500 cycles at 2C); High discharge capacity at extreme temperatures (912.7 mA h g−1 at 0.1C at −20 °C and 1350.7 mA h g−1 at 0.5C at 50 °C). Mechanism: The p-band center of the halogen anion shifts positively toward the Fermi level as the atomic number of the halogen increases, resulting in a higher charge transfer rate and promoting the kinetics of the conversion reaction of LiPSs. Quote: "the regulatory mechanism of halogen-induced p-band centers and their effects on the adsorption and catalytic performance of LSBs were successfully explored"
